question.:question/problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface generated by the vector-valued function

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\begin{pmatrix}u + v^{2}\\- u v\\u + v\end{pmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The fundamental vector product is $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$, in that order. Hold the other parameter constant in each partial derivative.

Differentiate the coordinates to obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(u + v^{2})&=1\\\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(- u v)&=- v\\\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(u + v)&=1\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(u + v^{2})&=2 v\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(- u v)&=- u\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(u + v)&=1\end{aligned}
$$

The tangent vectors are

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\begin{pmatrix}1\\- v\\1\end{pmatrix},\\\mathbf r_v&=\begin{pmatrix}2 v\\- u\\1\end{pmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the ordered determinant:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\1 & - v & 1\\2 v & - u & 1\end{vmatrix}.
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{1}&=(- v)(1)\\&\quad -(1)(- u)\\&=u - v.\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{2}&=-(1)(1)\\&\quad +(1)(2 v)\\&=2 v - 1.\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{3}&=(1)(- u)\\&\quad -(- v)(2 v)\\&=- u + 2 v^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{pmatrix}u - v\\2 v - 1\\- u + 2 v^{2}\end{pmatrix}.
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \begin{pmatrix}- u v + u\\2 v - 1\\2 u v^{2} - u\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}u^{2} + u v - v\\2 u v + 2 v^{2} - 1\\- u + 2 v^{2}\end{pmatrix}

generation.domain: all real u,v; zero products at singular parameters allowed

question.:question/problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface generated by the vector-valued function

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\begin{pmatrix}v\\v \sin{(u )}\\- u \cos{(v )}\end{pmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The fundamental vector product is $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$, in that order. Hold the other parameter constant in each partial derivative.

Differentiate the coordinates to obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(v)&=0\\\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(v \sin{(u )})&=v \cos{(u )}\\\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(- u \cos{(v )})&=- \cos{(v )}\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(v)&=1\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(v \sin{(u )})&=\sin{(u )}\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(- u \cos{(v )})&=u \sin{(v )}\end{aligned}
$$

The tangent vectors are

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\begin{pmatrix}0\\v \cos{(u )}\\- \cos{(v )}\end{pmatrix},\\\mathbf r_v&=\begin{pmatrix}1\\\sin{(u )}\\u \sin{(v )}\end{pmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the ordered determinant:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\0 & v \cos{(u )} & - \cos{(v )}\\1 & \sin{(u )} & u \sin{(v )}\end{vmatrix}.
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{1}&=(v \cos{(u )})(u \sin{(v )})\\&\quad -(- \cos{(v )})(\sin{(u )})\\&=u v \sin{(v )} \cos{(u )} + \sin{(u )} \cos{(v )}.\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{2}&=-(0)(u \sin{(v )})\\&\quad +(- \cos{(v )})(1)\\&=- \cos{(v )}.\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{3}&=(0)(\sin{(u )})\\&\quad -(v \cos{(u )})(1)\\&=- v \cos{(u )}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{pmatrix}u v \sin{(v )} \cos{(u )} + \sin{(u )} \cos{(v )}\\- \cos{(v )}\\- v \cos{(u )}\end{pmatrix}.
$$

generation.domain: all real u,v; zero products at singular parameters allowed

question.:question/problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface generated by the vector-valued function

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\begin{pmatrix}- u\\- u \sin{(v )}\\v \cos{(u )}\end{pmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The fundamental vector product is $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$, in that order. Hold the other parameter constant in each partial derivative.

Differentiate the coordinates to obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(- u)&=-1\\\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(- u \sin{(v )})&=- \sin{(v )}\\\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(v \cos{(u )})&=- v \sin{(u )}\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(- u)&=0\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(- u \sin{(v )})&=- u \cos{(v )}\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(v \cos{(u )})&=\cos{(u )}\end{aligned}
$$

The tangent vectors are

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\- \sin{(v )}\\- v \sin{(u )}\end{pmatrix},\\\mathbf r_v&=\begin{pmatrix}0\\- u \cos{(v )}\\\cos{(u )}\end{pmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the ordered determinant:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\-1 & - \sin{(v )} & - v \sin{(u )}\\0 & - u \cos{(v )} & \cos{(u )}\end{vmatrix}.
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{1}&=(- \sin{(v )})(\cos{(u )})\\&\quad -(- v \sin{(u )})(- u \cos{(v )})\\&=- u v \sin{(u )} \cos{(v )} - \sin{(v )} \cos{(u )}.\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{2}&=-(-1)(\cos{(u )})\\&\quad +(- v \sin{(u )})(0)\\&=\cos{(u )}.\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{3}&=(-1)(- u \cos{(v )})\\&\quad -(- \sin{(v )})(0)\\&=u \cos{(v )}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{pmatrix}- u v \sin{(u )} \cos{(v )} - \sin{(v )} \cos{(u )}\\\cos{(u )}\\u \cos{(v )}\end{pmatrix}.
$$

generation.domain: all real u,v; zero products at singular parameters allowed
